title: Anthropic shares end first day of trading at $97 as Wall Street closes sharply lower – business live
summary: All ⁠three major US stock indexes ⁠ended the session ​sharply lower after record-breaking IPO by maker behind AI agent Claude Anthropic needs to grow into its $1.5tn valuation, argues Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB: Anthropic’s triumphant IPO and its trillion dollar plus valuation is more typical of a mature company that has a history of strong fundamentals. title: Anthropic keeps the AI party swinging, but the atmosphere is bubbly | Nils Pratley
summary: Can the newly listed AI company really be worth $2tn? Anyone who remembers the late 1990s has good reason to ask Business live – latest updates Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company . From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees . Continue reading...

title: Protesters rally against Anthropic in New York and San Francisco after $2tn stock market debut
summary: Anti-AI groups gather in front of Nasdaq exchange in Times Square and Anthropic’s headquarters in San Francisco As the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic debuted on the US stock market at an eye-popping $2tn valuation Thursday, protesters from anti-AI groups rallied in front of the Nasdaq exchange at its New York City headquarters in Times Square and several were arrested. Similar demonstrations took place outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters. “I think people are starting to get that there’s something wrong,” Jose Gonzalez, 46, one of roughly 30 protesters in New York City, said. Protesters carried flags reading “STOP TECH OLIGARCHS” and “FREEZE AI: END ICE, END WAR”. Continue reading...

title: Academic integrity matters, but students shouldn’t be penalised for using AI | Letter
summary: Berthold Schoene responds after the head of Ofqual said students could be disqualified from GCSEs and A-levels if they tried to use AI in assessed coursework Is this really the best we can do: draconically penalise the young for making use of the latest cognitive resources and tools available to them ( Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat, 18 November )? Our generation has allowed the introduction of “life-altering” new technologies into every walk of life without much democratic debate, public scrutiny or governmental oversight. And now our education leaders are threatening to jeopardise young people’s career prospects for deploying these technologies within an education system that can’t cope and struggles to adapt? We all know that AI is here to stay. And importantly, it is so much more than just a cheap cheating device. Within an incredibly short space of time, it has transformed how we work, communicate, solve problems, research and learn. Surely the pedagogical response cannot simply be to devise ever more elaborate ways of preventing students from using it? Continue reading...
title_en: Academic integrity matters, but students shouldn't be penalised for using AI
title_zh: 学术诚信固然重要，但学生不应因使用AI而受罚
summary_en: A letter responds to Ofqual's threat of disqualification for AI use in coursework, arguing students shouldn't be penalised for using modern cognitive tools that education systems must adapt to rather than ban.
summary_zh: 一封读者来信回应英国资格考试局威胁取消在课程作业中使用AI的学生资格，认为不应惩罚学生使用现代认知工具，教育体系应适应而非禁止AI。
